The correct count is 36, so none of the three solutions is right.

The equation forces lcm(n,x) = 2n and gcd(n,y) = n. This requires x = 2·gcd(n,x) and n | y. Taking n = x/2 shows that a pair works exactly when x is even and (x/2) divides y. With d = x/2, the constraint x + y ≤ 20 becomes d(2 + t) ≤ 20 where y = dt.

| d | x | Valid y | Count |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 1–18 | 18 |
| 2 | 4 | even y ≤ 16 | 8 |
| 3 | 6 | 3, 6, 9, 12 | 4 |
| 4 | 8 | 4, 8, 12 | 3 |
| 5 | 10 | 5, 10 | 2 |
| 6 | 12 | 6 | 1 |

Total: 18 + 8 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 36. Odd x never works, since x = 2·gcd(n,x) forces x to be even.
